idiom_name: math.unit(value, name) / Unit.to() with built-in unit catalogue
implementation_notes: Plain JavaScript has no units and no operator overloading, so the pattern is a runtime library or a convention - and the library is the better deal. mathjs gives Unit objects where math.unit(45, 'cm') carries value plus unit, .to('cm') converts, add/multiply throw when the units do not match, createUnit() registers domain units, and the expression parser even understands '90 km/h to m/s'. It owns the unit catalogue, prefixes, affine offsets for temperatures and the arithmetic rules that a {value, unit} object with a switch statement would end up reimplementing badly. A hand-rolled factory is justified only for a handful of units and when the dependency (and its ~100 kB) is refused.
pitfalls: Units default to number storage, so chained conversions accumulate floating-point noise; wrap the magnitude in math.fraction or BigNumber when exactness matters.
Unit objects expose mutable-looking properties and are shared by reference, so treat them as immutable and never hand one to code that reassigns it; clone with .clone() when in doubt.
The unit string grammar is forgiving ('0.1 kilogram' parses), so misspelled unit names fail at run time only; construct from valueless Unit constants internally and validate user input at the edge.

variants.name: Hand-rolled frozen {value, unit} factory
variants.implementation_notes: Without a dependency, the honest manual form is a factory function returning a frozen plain object {value, unit} plus a single conversion table keyed by unit and dimension, with add/to helpers that throw on a dimension mismatch. Keep it tiny and closed: the moment compound units, prefixes or affine conversions appear, the hand-rolled table becomes the maintenance burden the library would have carried, so switch to a library there.
pitfalls: A unit that is not in the table silently produces undefined factors and NaN; validate the unit in the factory and throw.
Freezing the outer object does not freeze anything it references, so keep the shape primitive only (numbers and strings) or validate at the boundary.
The table scales badly: two dimensions or an affine unit and you are writing the library - switch to mathjs instead of growing this.
